title: Thresholdless corner vortex solitons in fractal Sierpiński topological insulators
authors: Yiqi Zhang, Alexander V. Kireev, Victor O. Kompanets, Sergey Y. Alyatkin, Nikita S. Kostyuchenko, Sergei A. Zhuravitskii, Nikolay N. Skryabin, Khalil Sabour, Alexander A. Kalinkin, Yongdong Li, Sergei P. Kulik, Pavlos G. Lagoudakis, Sergey V. Chekalin, Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Victor N. Zadkov
abstract: Quantized vortices are ubiquitous in physics, spanning superconductivity, astrophysics, superfluid condensed matter systems, and nonlinear optics. Yet embedding vorticity into topologically protected nonlinear states has remained a major challenge, with all previously observed corner solitons in higher-order topological insulators (HOTIs) exhibiting only trivial phase distributions. Here, we report on the first realization of stable topological corner vortex solitons in a photonic fractal HOTI. Using an array of laser-written waveguides in the shape of Sierpiński gasket with a controllable distortion, we design linear topological vortex modes, from which nonlinear corner vortex solitons bifurcate. Moreover, we demonstrate that these solitons exhibit exceptional robustness across a broad power range and, unlike vortex solitons in topologically trivial lattices, form without a power threshold. Our results introduce the angular momentum degree of freedom into the physics of topological corner modes, opening prospects for topologically protected vortex-based photonics.
summary: This paper reports the first experimental observation of stable topological corner vortex solitons within a photonic fractal Higher-Order Topological Insulator. By using a Sierpiński gasket waveguide array, the researchers demonstrated that these solitons form without a power threshold, confirming the introduction of angular momentum into the physics of topological corner modes.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is realizing and studying stable topological corner vortex solitons in photonic fractal Higher-Order Topological Insulators (HOTIs), overcoming the limitation that previous corner solitons only exhibited trivial phase distributions.
main_result: The authors report the first experimental realization of stable, topological corner vortex solitons in a photonic fractal HOTI, demonstrating their thresholdless formation and exceptional robustness across a wide power range.
method: The study combines theoretical analysis (solving the nonlinear Schrödinger equation) with experimental implementation using laser-written waveguide arrays to excite and measure the light confinement and phase structure.
model_or_system: The system is a photonic fractal HOTI realized using an array of laser-written waveguides shaped like a Sierpiński gasket. The physics is governed by the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and the topological properties are derived from the linear spectrum analysis.
key_observables: Output intensity distributions, phase structure (vortex singularity), and the existence of stable solitons across a broad power range.
important_parameters: The distortion parameter ($r$) of the fractal structure, the input power ($P$, tested from 0.01 MW to 3 MW), and the topological charge ($m=\pm 1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes standard normalizations for power and relies on the ability to construct linear corner vortex modes from degenerate corner doublets.
figures_summary: Figures show the Sierpiński gasket structure, the linear spectrum analysis (eigenvalues vs. mode index), the bifurcation of soliton families from linear states, and experimental measurements confirming the intensity confinement and phase singularity of the vortex solitons at various powers.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework (linear spectrum analysis and soliton bifurcation) to presenting the experimental setup and results, culminating in the confirmation of thresholdless, topologically protected vortex states.
why_interesting: This work bridges topological physics, nonlinear optics, and photonics, providing a concrete platform (photonic lattices) to study complex nonlinear wave phenomena like vortex solitons, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems research.
